businessRequirements.title: Only the six listed Voyager transactions are in scope
businessRequirements.statement: The Voyager Fleet context includes the six transactions listed in Petroleum chapter 9.

businessRequirements.title: Voyager uses Table Load card type 060
businessRequirements.statement: A Voyager fleet transaction uses card type 060 in the transaction Prompt Code when Voyager fleet processing is selected.

businessRequirements.title: Merchant Profile requires Terminal Special Code 073
businessRequirements.statement: The BUYPASS Merchant Profile must have Terminal Special Code 073 enabled for Voyager Fleet transactions.

businessRequirements.title: Fleet allowance uses Table Load or an alternate method
businessRequirements.statement: The POS application identifies Voyager card type 060 from Table Load or uses another method to determine whether Voyager fleet cards are allowed.

businessRequirements.title: Driver ID follows the magstripe prompt restriction
businessRequirements.statement: When the Voyager magstripe prompt restriction requires Driver ID, send unencrypted numeric data of 1 to 6 digits.

businessRequirements.title: Odometer follows the magstripe prompt restriction
businessRequirements.statement: When the Voyager magstripe prompt restriction requires odometer, it is numeric and 1 to 8 digits.

businessRequirements.title: Manual entry follows retry and account-entry requirements
businessRequirements.statement: After three unsuccessful reads, manual entry carries the 19-digit Voyager account, ISO number, expiry and Restriction Code in the source-defined order.
businessRequirements.interpretation: The distinct ISO-number prompt and the 19-digit account wording need confirmation before host serialization.

businessRequirements.title: Magstripe prompt Restriction Code is one of 0 through 3
businessRequirements.statement: The first Restriction Code digit is 0, 1, 2 or 3 and determines Driver ID and odometer prompting.

businessRequirements.title: Fuel restriction and Product Codes are enforced
businessRequirements.statement: The fuel Restriction Code distinguishes fuel-only from fuel-and-other-products processing; fuel-only transactions contain only fuel Product Codes.

businessRequirements.title: Product amounts equal the transaction amount
businessRequirements.statement: Product Code Data is present and product amounts sum to the transaction amount.

businessRequirements.title: Original magstripe transactions default to Track 2
businessRequirements.statement: Track 2 is the default card track for an original electronic Voyager Fleet transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Follow-on card data is partial Track 2
businessRequirements.statement: A follow-on transaction carries partial Track 2, except the stated TransArmor-VeriFone Edition full-Track-2 exception.

businessRequirements.title: Expiration date is validated
businessRequirements.statement: The device validates the expiration date on every Voyager Fleet transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Manual entry includes the ISO number
businessRequirements.statement: For manual entry, prompt for ISO Number and prefix it to the Voyager account number.

businessRequirements.title: Manual entry is marked on receipt and journal
businessRequirements.statement: Manual entry is marked by an asterisk before the account number on receipt and journal.

businessRequirements.title: Magstripe processing does not prompt Vehicle Number
businessRequirements.statement: Voyager magstripe transactions do not have a Vehicle Number prompt.

businessRequirements.title: Authorization amount processing follows request and CAT pump rules
businessRequirements.statement: The approved maximum amount is no greater than the Authorization Only request; POS authorization approval is based on the request amount.

businessRequirements.title: CAT authorization applies the pump-limit precedence rule
businessRequirements.statement: For CAT Authorization Only, the lower of approved maximum and AFP pump limit takes precedence.

businessRequirements.title: Fuel purchase types use unique Product Codes
businessRequirements.statement: Each type of fuel purchase has a unique Product Code in the transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Account Number Check Digit validates the account number
businessRequirements.statement: For POS processing, the Account Number Check Digit is a Mod 10 check over the account-number field; manual processing checks the first eight embossed digits.
businessRequirements.interpretation: The exact Mod 10 variant and manual-entry field boundaries need issuer/SME confirmation.

businessRequirements.title: Super Check Digit validates the full Voyager account data
businessRequirements.statement: The Super Check Digit is a Mod 10 check over the full ISO/account/card-identifier data; manual processing includes the ISO data.
businessRequirements.interpretation: The exact Mod 10 variant and manual-entry field boundaries need issuer/SME confirmation.

businessRequirements.title: Enhanced Fleet EMV identity is validated from Tag 9F6E
businessRequirements.statement: Enhanced Fleet is identified by Third Party Data unique identifier 0003 or 8003 and Product Identifier 0001.

businessRequirements.title: Voyager EMV application selection and AID are respected
businessRequirements.statement: The Voyager AID is A0000000049999C00016 and the Voyager Fleet payment application has priority 1 when multiple applications are supported.

businessRequirements.title: Premature card removal aborts and reverses if authorized
businessRequirements.statement: Removal before the terminal request aborts the transaction, and a reversal is sent if an authorization response was already received.

businessRequirements.title: Offline chip purchase restrictions are evaluated
businessRequirements.statement: Chip purchase restrictions and applicable offline fuel/non-fuel limits are checked before permitting products.

businessRequirements.title: Approved Voyager Chip receipts identify the selected application
businessRequirements.statement: Approved Voyager Chip receipts include the selected AID and the Application Preferred Name or Application Label.

businessRequirements.title: Swiped Voyager chip-capable cards request chip insertion
businessRequirements.statement: For Voyager EMV-capable cards, service code position 31 on Track 2 or position 58 on Track 1 is checked; a leading 2 or 6 prompts chip insertion.

businessRequirements.title: Terminal prompts follow Product Type bit priority
businessRequirements.statement: Without a Prompt Script File, enabled Voyager EMV prompts are presented in bit order 4, then 3, then 2, then 1.

businessRequirements.title: Abnormal chip declines retain troubleshooting evidence
businessRequirements.statement: The terminal stores the recommended chip and terminal-decision data for troubleshooting abnormal declines.

businessRequirements.title: Voyager Chip terminal is online capable
businessRequirements.statement: A Voyager terminal is online-only or offline-capable with online capability.

businessRequirements.title: Required Voyager terminal parameters are configured
businessRequirements.statement: Voyager Chip terminals support required application-wide terminal parameters, including Appendix L TAC values.

businessRequirements.title: CVM capabilities match attended terminal status
businessRequirements.statement: No CVM and online enciphered PIN are supported, offline PIN is not allowed, and signature is allowed only at attended terminals.

businessRequirements.title: Offline-capable terminal supports DDA and CDA
businessRequirements.statement: An offline-capable Voyager terminal supports both DDA and CDA; SDA is optional.

businessRequirements.title: Voyager EMV prompting uses Third Party Data
businessRequirements.statement: Voyager EMV prompt requirements are determined from Tag 9F6E Third Party Data.

businessRequirements.title: Voyager fleet account prefix is recognized
businessRequirements.statement: Voyager account-number prefix after ISO Number is one of 85, 86, 87, 88 or 89.

interpretations: Only POS Purchase and POS Authorization Only use exact transaction names in the ATL105 mapping; CAT, return and reversal mappings remain review-required.
Chapter 9 states Track 2 is the original default but does not state Track 1 fallback; Track 1 is catalogued but not treated as an established fallback.
The Voyager account and Super Check Digit checks are modeled with a provisional Mod 10/Luhn oracle; algorithm variant and field boundaries remain review-required.
EMV requirements are source-derived from chapter 9; Appendix I-L tables and the separate Voyager EMV terminal Specifications v1.5 remain out of scope.

testDataNotes: All account data, card identifiers, dates, prompt values and amounts are synthetic and are not source-example values.
The draft check-digit oracle uses the common Luhn/Mod 10 interpretation only to exercise the stated checks; issuer-specific algorithm behavior is not established.
Product codes come from Petroleum Appendix B; amounts are integer cents.
Voyager EMV test data is a logical source-rule fixture, not a TLV or host-serializable payload.

atl105Serialization.reason: A synthetic source-derived application-payload candidate now includes Segments 100, 101 and 102 and exercises their field delimiters and measured ASCII lengths. Existing Segment 101 and 102 logical validators accept its synthetic values. It is not output from the producer converter, host-tested, or an approval oracle; producer-compatible serialization and business validity remain unverified.
